hook: A section of the FBI's 62-HQ-83894 flying saucer case file spanning 1952–1954, containing an urgent field report of a saucer sighting over a nuclear AEC facility, J. Edgar Hoover's form letters routing civilian UFO reports to Air Force Intelligence, a translated German-language claim that flying saucers are Soviet V-weapons capable of carrying atom bombs, and an OSI colonel's confirmation that Wright-Patterson Field is the Air Force's UFO data correlation center.
why_it_matters: The sighting report at the Savannah River Plant—an active AEC nuclear production site—illustrates that UAP incidents at sensitive nuclear facilities were being logged at the FBI director level as early as 1952. The OSI colonel's statement explicitly naming Wright-Patterson as the central UFO evaluation point corroborates longstanding claims about that facility's role. The translated German letter, though anonymous, shows that foreign-origin propulsion theories (Soviet V-weapon) were being formally processed and translated by FBI cryptanalysis, reflecting how seriously the Bureau treated even speculative technical intelligence.

key_findings.finding: Two Du Pont Company employees reported a saucer-shaped blue light with an orange fringe flying at high speed over the Savannah River Plant's nuclear 'Four Hundred Area' on the evening of August 8, 1952, prompting an urgent FBI field cable to Hoover.

key_findings.finding: J. Edgar Hoover's office functioned as a forwarding bureau for civilian flying saucer reports, routing them to the Pentagon's Director of Special Investigations while explicitly closing each matter with a standard disclaimer of further FBI action.

key_findings.finding: An anonymous German-language letter, submitted to the Cincinnati FBI office and formally translated by the FBI's Cryptanalysis-Translation Section, claimed flying saucers are a Soviet-controlled V-weapon with a 48–50 meter disc diameter, 45–50 nozzles, atomic bomb payload capacity, and an intercontinental range of 30–35,000 km, allegedly confirmed by V-weapon constructor Riedel.

key_findings.finding: OSI District Commander Colonel S. W. Raynor confirmed to the Seattle FBI office that Wright-Patterson Field was the Air Force's UFO data correlation and evaluation center, while simultaneously stating OSI itself gave 'no credence whatsoever' to the reports and had no operational interest in them.

quotes.text: Colonel 8. W. RAYNOR, District Commander, OSI, states that there is an evaluation at Wright-Patterson Field where the data is correlated, that the reports are handled from the Air Foree here to that point in a routine fashion and that OSI gives no credence whatsoever to it because they have never had any previous experience of any kind as to anything arising out of the situation.
It is the opinion of Colonel RAYNOR that the releases are a poor thing and create mass hysteria, but he says he has nothing whatsoever to do with the situation.

key_findings.finding: The FBI's San Diego office was collecting materials from and surveilling Borderland Sciences Research Associates, a civilian UFO research organization with directors Mead Layne and Max Freedom Long, obtained through a member named Francis Ohm.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: OSI Colonel Raynor explicitly names Wright-Patterson Field as the central Air Force facility for correlating and evaluating UFO report data.
The urgent Savannah field cable reports a saucer sighting directly over the Savannah River Plant, an active AEC nuclear production facility operated by Du Pont.

Hoover's routing letters consistently forward civilian reports to the Pentagon's Director of Special Investigations for Air Force handling, the institutional predecessor to Project Blue Book's intake process.

The Savannah River Plant was an AEC nuclear facility in the same national laboratory network as Oak Ridge, and the sighting there mirrors Oak Ridge photographic incidents referenced in the broader case file description.
